native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (Copper/Gold + Amber + Monument Count) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400-1301 BCE) at a mean of 4.24 z-units. The peak was driven by a major increase in Copper/Gold (z 1.08 to 2.54, delta +1.46) and a substantial increase in Monument Count (z 0.93 to 1.71, delta +0.78) relative to the 15th century BCE. Amber increased only marginally (z -0.08 to -0.01, delta +0.07), remaining near zero. Copper/Gold and Monument Count were the dominant individual components increasing toward the social capital maximum.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE -4100 to -500). Used interpolated Z-score columns CopperGold_inter, Amber_inter, MonumentCount_inter. Computed unweighted sum per year. Converted CE to BCE centuries via ceil(-CE/100). Grouped by century, took mean of summed social capital, identified peak century (14th c. BCE, mean=4.24). Compared component means between 15th and 14th c. BCE to identify increases. Cross-checked with capital.csv (fixed comma decimals, summed ZCU_AU+Zamber+ZMonument): confirmed same 14th c. BCE peak. Sensitivity with 5 components (added Depot_inter, MonumentSize_inter) shifts peak to 12th c. BCE.

sub_hypo.text: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously while summer social capital peaks.
sub_hypo.relations: Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously, coinciding with a peak in summer social capital. No column corresponding to summer social capital is identified in the supplied metadata.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?

sub_hypo.text: Summed social capital, defined as Copper/Gold + Amber + Monument Count, peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE) at a century mean of 4.24 z-units.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological annual time series spanning CE -4100 to -500, aggregated into BCE centuries using ceil(-CE/100).
sub_hypo.relations: The unweighted annual sum of the three interpolated Z-score components was averaged by century; its maximum century mean was 4.24 in the 14th century BCE.

sub_hypo.text: Copper/Gold and Monument Count were the dominant individual components increasing toward the social capital maximum, while Amber increased only marginally and remained near zero.
sub_hypo.context: Comparison of component century means between the 15th and 14th centuries BCE in the archaeological time series.
sub_hypo.relations: Copper/Gold increased from 1.08 to 2.54 z-units (+1.46), Monument Count from 0.93 to 1.71 (+0.78), and Amber from -0.08 to -0.01 (+0.07). Copper/Gold and Monument Count contributed the dominant increases in the summed social capital.

sub_hypo.text: The capital.csv cross-check confirmed the same 14th-century BCE peak for three-component summed social capital.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological capital data, with comma decimals corrected before summing the three social capital components.
sub_hypo.relations: The sum ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument confirmed the 14th-century BCE peak.

sub_hypo.text: Expanding the social capital sum to five components by adding Depot and Monument Size shifted the peak to the 12th century BCE.
sub_hypo.context: Sensitivity analysis of the archaeological time series using five rather than three components.
sub_hypo.relations: Adding Depot_inter and MonumentSize_inter to the three-component sum shifted the peak century from the 14th to the 12th century BCE.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Summed social capital (Copper/Gold + Amber + Monument Count) peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400-1301 BCE) at a mean of 4.24 z-units. The peak was driven by a major increase in Copper/Gold (z 1.08 to 2.54, delta +1.46) and a substantial increase in Monument Count (z 0.93 to 1.71, delta +0.78) relative to the 15th century BCE. Amber increased only marginally (z -0.08 to -0.01, delta +0.07), remaining near zero. Copper/Gold and Monument Count were the dominant individual components increasing toward the social capital maximum.
